transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-11-20
Time: 14:00 PST
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Emily Carter (Redwood AE), Daniel Ruiz (Redwood SE), Alex Morgan (VectorPay - Head of ML), Priya Shah (VectorPay - Infra Lead), Tom Ellis (VectorPay - Procurement)

AUTO-GENERATED SUMMARY (brief, may be noisy):
VectorPay is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for payment fraud models and customer support assistant. Primary drivers: isolation/data controls, predictable throughput, and cost per token under heavy peak loads. They have a hybrid infra footprint across us-west and gcp-europe, need burst strategy for peak transaction windows, and want SOC2 + KMS requirements validated. Next steps include pricing/sizing, benchmark plan, and pilot kickoff.

TOPICS:
- current stack and models (huggingface transformer variants, some finetuned LLaMA family)
- expected qps and burst patterns
- isolation requirements (dedicated GPU pools / tenancy)
- autoscale / burst / overcommit policies
- security: SOC2, KMS, VPC peering, audit logs
- success criteria and timeline

TRANSCRIPT:
[00:00] Emily: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. This is Emily from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, with me is Daniel, our SE, and we're here to understand VectorPay's needs for Dedicated capacity.
[00:18] Alex: Hi, Alex here. Thanks. Quick context on our side, we run fraud scoring and a customer chat assistant. We want to move away from managed public endpoints because of token billing and data isolation concerns.
[00:32] Daniel: Cool, and real quick, are you currently running models in GCP or AWS for inference? Just to get a sense of networking and VPC needs.
[00:40] Priya: Mostly GCP, we have a couple of regions — us-west1 for production and europe-west1 for EU traffic. We have an on-prem sandbox for compliance tests.
[00:50] Alex: Our fraud model is a finetuned LLaMA-2 derivative, 13B quantized for cost. The chat assistant is a smaller 7B. Peak windows are 9am-11am PST and 6pm-8pm PST depending on partner batch runs.
[01:12] Emily: Helpful. So the Dedicated product gives you reserved GPU pools that are isolated per customer and you can size them for steady-state and configure burst policies for peaks. We can discuss burst capacity details but first what's your target 99th percentile latency and expected token volumes?
[01:30] Priya: 99p latency target is around 200-250ms for the chat assistant, fraud can tolerate up to 500ms for scoring but throughput is important during partner batches. Token volume is spiky; average qps is maybe 8-12 but bursts up to 120 qps for short periods — like 10-15 minutes.
[01:50] Daniel: Ok that's a pretty spiky profile. For Dedicated we typically size baseline pools for steady-state and then have a burst lane that can auto-scale. One note — bursts are typically handled by either reserved burst capacity or overflow to a compatible hosted tier; do you have any constraints about falling back to hosted?
[02:10] Alex: We prefer not to fall back to public hosted endpoints for data residency reasons; data can't leave our VPC. So any overflow needs to be within Dedicated or Private options.
[02:22] Emily: Understood. We can do Dedicated with private networking (VPC peering) so traffic stays within your network. We also have Private deployments for fully customer-managed control plane if you need on-prem. Any compliance constraints pushing you to Private versus Dedicated?
[02:40] Priya: SOC2 is mandatory, and we need KMS integration for keys. We also need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. Dedicated with managed control plane is acceptable as long as we can integrate KMS and get the audit logs.
[02:55] Daniel: We support customer-managed KMS and audit logs for Dedicated customers. There are some config steps for peering and IAM. We'll share the security pack that walks through the SAML/SSO, KMS, and audit export.
[03:10] Tom: Procurement question — what's the minimum commitment for Dedicated? We run quarterly budgets.
[03:16] Emily: Typically we do monthly or annual reserved capacity. The commitment can be sized for baseline and you can add burst credits. We'll include flexible billing options in the pricing doc.
[03:28] Alex: On the model side, do you have kernel-level optimizations for quantized LLaMA variants? We care about perf at 13B quantized.
[03:38] Daniel: Yes, our runtime picks optimized kernels and can run int8/4 quantized variants; performance depends on sequence lengths and KV cache hit rates. For 13B quantized we often see good throughput on A100/RTX-class GPUs and we can share benchmarks. We'll want to benchmark with your exact prompt set.
[03:56] Priya: We also have strict cold start requirements; if a model hasn't been used for 30 minutes it should spin up within X seconds — what are typical startup times?
[04:08] Daniel: Cold start can vary; for a 13B quantized model on dedicated GPU pool it's usually in the single-digit seconds for loading weights if the model is pinned and cache warm. If everything needs to be provisioned from zero it can be longer. We have warm pool options to avoid long cold starts.
[04:28] Alex: Can you explain warm pool and cache behaviour? We've seen KV cash — sorry KV cache — misunderstandings in other vendors.
[04:36] Daniel: Sure. We keep KV caches for recent sequences per session and we do prefix caching for common prompts. Warm pool means some fraction of GPUs keep models resident so first token latency stays low. For fraud scoring we can pin the model on a set of workers to ensure predictable 99p.
[04:52] Emily: Quick qual question — timeline for pilot and success criteria?
[04:58] Alex: We want pilot in December, procurement signoff ideally end of November. Success criteria: 99p latency under 250ms for chat, throughput during burst without errors, and validated security controls (KMS, SOC2, logs). Also cost per 1M tokens should be below our current vanity numbers — we'll share current effective cost.
[05:20] Daniel: That aligns. For pilot we'll propose a week-long performance run with your prompts, and a canary deployment for real traffic. We'll provide a recommended sizing chart.
[05:30] Priya: Networking — we need VPC peering and peering IP ranges. Does Redwood support private connectivity to GCP?
[05:38] Emily: Yes, we support VPC peering and private interconnects for major clouds; there are firewall rules and routing steps. We'll circulate a network prep doc.
[05:48] Tom: On billing, if we buy reserved capacity and then don't use all of it during a month is there roll-over?
[05:55] Emily: There's some flexibility depending on contract; we can discuss buffer credits and burst pools. We'll put options in the offer.
[06:04] Alex: For high availability across regions: if us-west capacity is exhausted can we failover to europe? We need to keep EU PII inside EU for some transactions.
[06:15] Daniel: Smart routing policies can route by region and model variant. For EU PII you can pin traffic to the EU cluster and block cross-region failover for that subset. For other traffic you can allow fallback.
[06:30] Priya: Sequence lengths for fraud scoring are short, typically under 128 tokens, but chat sessions go up to 1024 tokens for some transcripts. How does that affect cost/perf?
[06:41] Daniel: Longer sequences increase memory use and can reduce throughput; batching strategy matters. For chat we usually recommend smaller batch windows and KV cache to reduce repeated compute. We'll include quantization recommendations per workload.
[06:56] Alex: Any customers with similar profile (payments + compliance) you can reference?
[07:02] Emily: We have a couple fintech customers in pilot, can't share PII but we can connect you to references under NDA.
[07:09] Tom: Ok procurement will want a legal checklist — standard SLAs, data handling, termination terms.
[07:15] Emily: We'll include a term sheet and SLA options.
[07:20] Alex: Regarding burst strategy: you mentioned either reserved burst GPUs or overflow to hosted; since overflow isn't allowed, can we overcommit baseline and buy burst pool at some premium?
[07:32] Daniel: Yes, typical patterns: (1) baseline reserved pool sized for steady qps, (2) reserved burst pool that remains idle but can be used for short windows, and (3) autoscale with fast warm pools. There's a tradeoff on cost vs unused capacity. We'll model your 10-15 minute spikes and show cost comparisons.
[07:50] Priya: What's the expected time to scale the burst pool if we see sudden load?
[07:55] Daniel: With warm pool pre-warmed, scaling can be within tens of seconds. If new instances need to be provisioned we should expect a few minutes; that's why we recommend warm pool sizing for predictable bursts.
[08:10] Alex: For data retention and logs, can we set retention windows for transcripts and tokens? We want a 30-day default and then archive.
[08:20] Emily: Yes configurable retention and we can set up automatic exports to your storage.
[08:26] Tom: On security, does Redwood rotate keys if we use customer-managed KMS?
[08:31] Daniel: Key rotation can be controlled by your KMS policy. We don't hold plaintext keys; encryption at rest is managed by customer KMS.
[08:40] Alex: For the benchmark, what telemetry will you capture? We need traces tied to tokens, per-route latency, and cost breakdowns.
[08:48] Daniel: We'll run our profiler and provide per-token latency, batching efficiency, GPU utilization, and token cost estimation. We'll also provide logs you can ingest into your systems.
[08:58] Priya: One more on multi-tenant isolation — do you use strict tenancy or soft isolation on Dedicated?
[09:06] Emily: Dedicated provides tenant-isolated GPU pools; the control plane is shared but network and compute are isolated. For full on-prem isolation, Private is the option but it's heavier.
[09:18] Alex: Ok, can you walk through an example sizing for our burst profile?
[09:22] Daniel: Sure — if baseline is 10 qps with 128 tokens per request, we compute tokens/sec and map to GPU throughput. For bursts to 120 qps we'd recommend X number of A100s as burst pool. We'll put exact numbers in the sizing doc after we get your real traffic histogram.
[09:40] Emily: Priya, can you share traffic histograms? That helps us avoid overprovisioning.
[09:45] Priya: I'll export and send the last 30 days. Expect it by Friday.
[09:50] Alex: Another subtlety: our fraud pipeline needs deterministic inference for scoring reproducibility. Does Redwood support pinned model versions and model immutability for audit?
[10:02] Daniel: Yes, you can pin model versions and we have versioned deployments and immutable model artifacts for rollbacks and audit.
[10:10] Tom: Procurement curiosity — do you offer a trial contract with small committed baseline?
[10:16] Emily: Yes, pilot contracts are common: a short-term reserved small baseline plus performance acceptance criteria and a path to full reserved.
[10:24] Alex: Are there any known limitations with GPUs you recommend for quantized 13B models? Memory or kernel support?
[10:32] Daniel: Lower-memory GPUs can limit batch sizes; some quantization backends may require specific CUDA/kernel versions. We'll map that out and recommend GPUs. For dedicated we support a variety and can tailor.
[10:42] Priya: For compliance we may want SOC2 + ISO27001. Do you have ISO?
[10:48] Emily: We are SOC2 Type II and in process for ISO27001; security pack will clarify timelines and attestations.
[10:55] Alex: Great. For the pilot can we request a short run across EU region with masked data?
[11:02] Daniel: Absolutely, masked or synthetic data is recommended and we'll support region-specific deployments.
[11:09] Priya: Network ops question: do you support peering with our on-prem test environment?
[11:14] Emily: Yes, we can support VPN/Private Interconnects for on-prem. We'll add network runbook.
[11:20] Tom: Any dependencies we should flag to legal? Data processing addendum?
[11:26] Emily: We'll include DPA and standard terms; we can iterate with your legal.
[11:32] Alex: Ok, let's recap next steps.
[11:36] Emily: We'll share the pricing/sizing spreadsheet, security pack, and a proposed benchmark plan. Daniel will draft the benchmark and test harness. Priya will share traffic histograms. Tom will share procurement window and PO process.
[11:54] Daniel: I'll also include a list of recommended GPUs and warm pool sizing options, plus a runbook for VPC peering.
[12:03] Alex: Sounds good. Anything else?
[12:06] Priya: No, that's it from infra.
[12:08] Tom: Thanks all.
[12:10] Emily: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the docs and a proposed pilot kickoff slot for week of 11/24.

(end of transcript)
